answer: For a pearl-trading agent network spanning a delta and a canyon, admission requires storing a distinct random 64 MB shard for a day. Commit its hash before a public beacon selects unpredictable byte ranges to audit. Missing a timed proof cancels that identity's reward. Bind each shard to its public key, so one stored copy cannot serve many aliases. A thousand identities require roughly 64 GB plus audit bandwidth; set rewards below measured rental cost. This prices duplication, not proves unique ownership.
